title: Pre-mortem: The Neuroscience of Avoiding Disaster
thread: I once broke into my own home at -40°C. The reason? I forgot my passport the next morning. Neuroscience explains why—and how to prevent it.
Under stress, cortisol floods your brain, impairing rational thought. You won't be at your best when it matters most. So plan ahead.
The fix: a 'pre-mortem.' Imagine your failure and work backward. Ask: What could go wrong? Then set up safeguards.
Simple hacks: designate spots for keys, passport, glasses. Photograph important documents and email them to yourself. Your hippocampus will thank you.

For medical decisions, ask: What's the NNT (number needed to treat)? For statins, 300 people take it for a year to prevent one heart attack. Side effects hit 5%—that's 15 people harmed for every one helped.
You're 15x more likely to be harmed than helped by statins. That doesn't mean don't take them—but you deserve to know the numbers.
We all have flaws. Pre-mortems help you anticipate failures and reduce damage. As the speaker said, 'Organization is a gradual process.' Start today.
